# War Scroll Column 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 16 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**1** [...] the priests will sound the trumpets [...] to arrange the battle formations [...]

**2** [...] and on the rally trumpets they will sound a long blast to direct the fighting [...]

**3** [...they will begin] to strike down the enemy. All the troops will stop their battle cry, but the priests will keep sounding

**4** the trumpets over the slain to guide the fighting, until the enemy is cut down and turns

**5** to flee. The priests will sound the trumpets to direct the battle. When the enemy is driven back

**6** before them, the priests will sound the trumpets for assembly, and all the front-line soldiers will advance

**7** toward them through the fallen of the vanguard, while six fresh divisions take their stand. The division going forward

**8** fully armed will take up its assigned position. Six additional divisions will move into place,

**9** making twenty-six divisions in all. The cavalry will take positions on the right and left flanks

**10** of the battle line: six hundred riders on each side.

**11** When Belial arms himself to aid the forces of Darkness, and casualties mount among the foot soldiers

**12** through God's hidden purposes — testing everyone chosen for battle — the priests

**13** will sound the call-up trumpets for a relief column to go forward and take the place of the fallen

**14** [...] and the priests will signal them to form up their ranks [...]

**15** [...] and when the priests sound the call [...] to test through these divine purposes [...all those chosen]

**16** for war [...] and the mighty fighters of [...] the battle [...] the God of Israel [...]

**17** [...] for every appointed time throughout eternity [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 16 details the tactical coordination between priests and soldiers during the final engagements. Heavy damage to the top and bottom of the column. "Mysteries" rendered as "hidden purposes" / "divine purposes" to convey the theological concept accessibly. Military terminology modernized for clarity.*
